newsitem.title: NORWAY: Cruise passengers call Arctic groundings adventure.
newsitem.headline: Cruise passengers call Arctic groundings adventure.

text.p: A day after their cruise liner was rescued from a sandbank off Norway's Spitzbergen island, elderly German holidaymakers described their four-day ordeal as 'a bit of an adventure'.
The German-owned cruiser Hanseatic arrived in Longyear, a village of 1,100 tucked between a mountain and a fjord, on Friday morning after a 14-hour journey from the northern coast of Spitzbergen
The 145 passengers, mostly German and with an average age of 70, were taken off shortly before the 9,000 deadweight-ton liner was dragged off the sandbank on Thursday by a Norwegian coastguard ship.

The coastguard ship sailed up to the side of the Hanseatic and took on board the holidaymakers before refloating it. They were later allowed to return to the Hanseatic, which was being examined for seaworthiness on Friday in Longyear.
"We never felt the situation was dramatic," German passenger Renate Weyer told the Norwegian news agency NTB.
"I think most of us saw this as a big adventure."

Norwegian officials held a meeting with Hanseatic captain Hartvig von Harling while passengers went on bus tours of Longyear, Elisabeth Aarsaether, spokeswoman for the governor's office at Longyear on Spitzbergen, told Reuters.
She said the ship's owner, Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd AG, had decided not to fly back the passengers to Hamburg but to carry on the journey as originally planned to Reykjavik, Iceland.
